items.title: 8.4 Dynamic equilibrium between two physical states

source_refs.note: Topic 8.4, printed pages 170-171, with Quick Check 8.2 as the self-check.

blocks.title: Dynamic equilibrium
blocks.text: Dynamic equilibrium is a state in a reversible process where the rate of change in one direction equals the rate of change in the opposite direction: although changes keep taking place, no net change in the system as a whole is observed.
A reversible phase change also gives a dynamic equilibrium between two physical states: at 0 degrees C ice and water coexist, water changing into ice and ice back into water at the same rate.

When a liquid is placed in a closed container, some liquid molecules near the surface have enough energy to escape into the gas phase, evaporation; as more molecules escape, the pressure of the gas on the walls increases. At the same time vapour molecules collide with the liquid surface and are captured again, condensation. As the two processes continue their rates become equal and dynamic equilibrium is reached: the number of liquid molecules becoming gas equals the number of gas molecules returning to liquid, and the vapour pressure stays constant at a given temperature as long as the system is undisturbed. Raising the temperature raises the average kinetic energy of the liquid molecules, so evaporation is faster and the vapour pressure rises; condensation also speeds up, and a new dynamic equilibrium is reached with a higher equilibrium vapour pressure. Dynamic equilibrium in terms of vapour pressure is the state at which the rates of evaporation and condensation are equal.

blocks.prompt: Justify that a dynamic equilibrium exists between water and its vapour at 100 degrees C, and between ice and water at 0 degrees C.
blocks.explanation: At 100 degrees C in a closed vessel water evaporates and its vapour condenses at equal rates, so the vapour pressure stays at 1 atm while molecules keep crossing the surface both ways: a dynamic equilibrium. At 0 degrees C ice melts and water freezes at the same rate, so the amounts of ice and water stay constant although individual molecules keep changing state; this too is dynamic.

items: Dynamic equilibrium: opposite changes at equal rates, no net change; ice and water at 0 degrees C; liquid and vapour in a closed vessel, where evaporation equals condensation and the vapour pressure is constant, rising to a new equilibrium value at higher temperature.
